title: Do LLMs Change Their Minds Like Humans? Diagnosing Human--LLM Divergence in Single-Turn Persuasion Judgments
abstract: arXiv:2608.29803v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as proxies for human participants in social simulations, yet whether they update their beliefs in response to persuasive arguments, as humans do, remains poorly understood. We conduct a systematic comparison using a naturally occurring online persuasion corpus in which original posters explicitly verify whether a reply changed their view. Our results show that LLMs achieve only slight agreement with humans (Cohen's kappa ranging from 0.079 to 0.178). Content-level analyses show that humans and LLMs agree on the strongest persuasion cues but diverge on finer ones: humans are more swayed by novel content and assertive language, whereas LLMs favor topical similarity and surface-level formatting. translated_title: 大语言模型会像人类一样改变想法吗？诊断单轮说服判断中人类与大语言模型的分歧
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）在社会模拟中越来越多地被用作人类参与者的替代品，但它们是否会像人类一样在说服性论据面前更新自己的信念，目前仍知之甚少。我们利用一个自然产生的在线说服语料库进行了系统性比较，在该语料库中，原帖作者会明确验证回复是否改变了他们的观点。结果表明，大语言模型与人类仅达到轻微的一致性（Cohen's kappa 系数介于 0.079 至 0.178 之间）。内容层面的分析显示，人类与大语言模型在最强的说服线索上意见一致，但在较细微的线索上存在分歧：人类更容易被新颖的内容和断言性的语言所打动，而大语言模型则更看重主题相似性和表面层面的格式。在说服策略层面，与人类相比，大语言模型低估了情感诉求的作用，却高估了可信度信号的作用，而所讨论命题的类型并未产生可测量的影……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该研究通过真实的在线说服数据发现，大语言模型在判断“回复是否改变了发帖人观点”时与人类仅存在微弱一致性，人类更易被新颖内容和断言性语言说服，而大语言模型更看重主题相似性与表面格式，且相对低估情感诉求、高估可信度信号。
en_tdlr: Using a naturalistic online persuasion corpus, this study shows that LLMs achieve only slight agreement with humans (Cohen's kappa 0.079–0.178) in single-turn persuasion judgments—humans are swayed more by novel content and assertive language, while LLMs favor topical similarity and surface formatting, underweighting emotional appeals and overweighting credibility signals.
